### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via handleCatalogActivationWrite (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **51** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f48aa45102fe34621b04f1ddd1d8defe765c797e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `46ae06fb508f7be35f2639d056dbe018f620b18c` — the merge of head `c5672b2ff3170b11539e6c8c562c761f7f972379` into base `f48aa45102fe34621b04f1ddd1d8defe765c797e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 46ae06fb508f7be35f2639d056dbe018f620b18c && git checkout 46ae06fb508f7be35f2639d056dbe018f620b18c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f48aa45102fe34621b04f1ddd1d8defe765c797e c5672b2ff3170b11539e6c8c562c761f7f972379 && git checkout -B drift-repro f48aa45102fe34621b04f1ddd1d8defe765c797e && git merge --no-ff c5672b2ff3170b11539e6c8c562c761f7f972379

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f48aa45102fe34621b04f1ddd1d8defe765c797e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f48aa45102fe34621b04f1ddd1d8defe765c797e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c5672b2ff3170b11539e6c8c562c761f7f972379`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #26474 (body and all 6 comments: triage `6434156905`, claim `6434820232`, ruling `6434876664`, amended claim `6434884699`, spec handoff `6436285999`, dev report `6436600379`), PR #26551 body and 16-file list, `git diff origin/main...c5672b2f` (394+/40-), cited code read with `git show` at the head, and the head's check-runs (read 2026-10-27T07:55Z and again 2026-10-27T08:01Z).

### ① Derived judgments

**Public-surface changes the diff implies**

1. `@objectstack/core` — `MetadataActivationStore.setActive(row, options?)`: an optional second parameter on a published interface. Callers may now pass it, implementers need not change. **Right** (widening, additive).
2. `@objectstack/core` — `ObjectStoreMetadataActivationStore.setActive` and `InMemoryMetadataActivationStore.setActive` take the same optional parameter; the in-memory store ignores it and says so. **Right.**
3. `@objectstack/core` — new exported types `MetadataActivationWriteContext` (`{ readonly isSystem: true; readonly userId?: string } & Record<string, unknown>`) and `MetadataActivationWriteOptions`, reachable through `export * from './utils/metadata-activation-store.js'` (`packages/core/src/index.ts:187`). The `isSystem: true` literal in the type is the compile-time guard; the store has no runtime `isSystem` read, which is what keeps `check:system-context-census` green. **Right.**
4. `@objectstack/objectql` — `ObjectQL.setActionActive(row, options?)`, `ActionActivationProjection.setActive(row, options?)`, and the type export `ActionActivationWriteOptions` from `index.ts`. `packages/spec` declares no `setActionActive` on `IObjectQLEngine` (grep at the head: no hit), so no spec change is owed and the lane red line holds; runtime calls it through `ql: any`. **Right.**
5. `@objectstack/runtime` — `activationWriteContext` is internal: `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` exports nothing from `domains/` and `package.json` exposes only `"."`. Runtime publishes a behaviour change, no surface change. **Right.**

**Accept-set changes.** The two HTTP doors (`POST /api/v1/actions/_activation/:object/:action`, `POST /api/v1/security/_activation/:type/:name`) keep the same body reader, gates, declaration lookup and status pairs; their accept-set is unchanged. The store and engine accept-set widens by the optional `{ context }`. Absent, the store keeps `SYSTEM_CTX` (pinned by the no-caller control). **Right.**

**The write context `{ ...callerContext, isSystem: true }` (the brief's extra question)**

- *Ordering.* Both doors build it only at the write step, after `refuseUngrantedActivationAuthoring` and `refuseUngrantedActivationWrite` admitted the caller: `actions.ts` step 1 then step 5; `catalog-activation.ts:237,239` then the write at `:399-405`. Neither gate is touched by the diff.
- *Nothing newly admitted.* The engine's `isSystem` bypasses RBAC, RLS and FLS (`engine.ts:9704`), exactly as the old constant `SYSTEM_CTX` did, and `{ ...context, isSystem: true }` is the engine's own documented `sudo()` shape (`engine.ts:9707`, `:12892-12916`). A caller the gates refuse never reaches the write; a caller they admit was already elevated to the full system write before this PR. No permission or tenancy check that was enforced before is skipped now.
- *Tenancy.* `sys_metadata_activation` declares `systemFields: { tenant: false }` (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-metadata-activation.object.ts:112`) and the registry honours the opt-out (`registry.ts:876`, `:1208`). So the caller's `organizationId` neither tenant-filters the keyed read (the read-then-write stays keyed on type + name; no duplicate-row risk) nor stamps a tenant column on the ledger row (`plugin.ts:1600` is gated on `hasField(objectName, 'tenant_id')`).
- *Actor recorded, not hand-stamped.* The diff's source files assign no `created_by`, `updated_by`, `user_id` or `actor` literal. The ledger row's stamps are the engine's `sys_stamp_audit_*` hooks (`plugin.ts:1594-1597`, keyed on `session?.userId`, no `isSystem` exemption, `session` being `hookCtx.session` from the write's context). The audit row's are the audit plugin's `user_id: userId ?? null` and `actor = userId ?? sess.actor` with `userId = sess.userId ?? attributedUserId` (`audit-writers.ts:2016`, `:2125`, actorLabel). Both read the same context the door handed down, so the actor is the caller's. **Right.**
- *Residual observation, not a finding.* With no `executionContext` the helper yields a bare `{ isSystem: true }` without `positions: []` / `permissions: []`; that shape is unreachable past the two gates and the engine takes it elsewhere.

**Tests and pins.** The new pins are the right ones: the core store's `find`/`insert`/`update` contexts and the no-caller control; objectql pass-through; both runtime doors handing down exactly `{ ...executionContext, isSystem: true }` (tenant admin under `single`, operator under `isolated`; the catalog door on insert and the later update); dogfood on a real engine plus `AuditPlugin` for both rows, off then on. The dogfood harness surface it uses exists (`BootOptions.extraPlugins` `harness.ts:511`, `signIn` `:170`, `apiAs` `:176`). The five existing `toHaveBeenCalledWith` pins relaxed to `expect.anything()` pin the row, not the context, and the new describes pin the context. **Right.** Red-first is claimed with commit order (`6eed608a`, `2e0d5df6` before `773a999a`) and per-suite failure text; read as claimed, not re-run.

**Gate verdicts on the head** (2026-10-27T08:01Z): 46 check-runs: 28 `success`, 8 `skipped`, 0 `failure`, 10 `in_progress`. Still running: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/8)` through `(7/8)`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace`. Completed green include `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, all `Lint ·` lanes, `Type Check · consumer gates` / `debt ledger` / `source gates`, `Test Core (8/8)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (its PR-side no-op).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/26474-activation-ledger-actor.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`. `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true`, so no changeset is owed for the new dogfood file. The three packages are exactly the ones the diff publishes from. **Matches.**
- Level rule (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3): the level follows the Metadata-protocol kind alone; `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The diff changes no metadata key, value or type. **`patch` right.**
- Declarations: PR body and changeset body both carry, line-initial, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. `yes (widening)` is a well-formed arm of the closed pair; `yes` is right because the published store/engine accept-set widens and nothing narrows or breaks. `Check Changeset` is `success`.
- Clause-②: yes (widening)

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` in report `6436600379`. None to answer.
- Dev flag — flow door still null-actor (`out_of_scope_findings[0]`): **answered.** The open half of #26474 behind spec card #26506 per ruling `6434876664`; the PR says `Part of #26474` and the `Part-of PR must not also close its card` run is green. The spec handoff `6436285999` names 18 pins in 8 runtime test files and three stale docblocks for the flow half; none of those files is in this PR's list, so nothing there is owed here. The card takes `Blocked-by: #26506` / `pm:blocked` once this lands, per the ruling's item 2.
- Dev flag — audit row `tenant_id` now carries the caller's organization (`out_of_scope_findings[1]`, carrier none): **answered, accepted, no card owed.** Confirmed in code: `audit-writers.ts` sets `tenantId = recordOrgId ?? sess.organizationId`, and the ledger row has no organization column, so the activation audit row's `tenant_id` becomes the acting admin's organization. Effect: under the `sys_audit_log_org` row policy that row is readable to organization readers of the admin's own organization instead of platform admins only. Reachable only under `single`, since under wall-enforcing postures `refuseUngrantedActivationWrite` admits `PLATFORM_ADMIN` alone (`activation-gate.ts`). This is ADR-0131 D7's own meaning of the column (the organization the row is about) and is recorded in the PR's Acceptance notes; it is not escalated.
- Dev flag — clone-as-`system` side note (`out_of_scope_findings[2]`): **answered.** Ruling `6434876664` item 3 carries it on the `registerAndSaveFlow` / `PutOptions.actor` path; not this PR.
- Dev flag — the first sweep's `check:system-context-census` red: **answered.** Resolved in `c5672b2f` by dropping the store's runtime `isSystem` read; the head's store has none, and the census lane is green on the head.
- Dev flag — CI in progress at report time: **recorded above**; ten runs were still in progress at review time, none had failed. The seat's adoption follows their completion.
- The dev report's earlier copy on #25235 is ignored per the brief.
